title: Vanishing of the positive cohomology of the reduction modulo an ideal spreads to all power-torsion and bounded complexes with power-torsion cohomology
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, and an object K of D(R) with H^i(K tensor^L_R R/I) = 0 for i > 0, and asserts three things: that H^i(K tensor^L_R R/I^n) = 0 for all n >= 1 and i > 0; that H^i(K tensor^L_R N) = 0 for any I-power torsion module N and i > 0; and that for any bounded complex M whose cohomology modules are I-power torsion and vanish in positive degrees one has H^i(K tensor^L_R M) = 0 for i > 0 (source lines 24109-24122). The proof works by reduction. For part (2) it writes N as the union of the submodules N[I^n] and uses that tensor products commute with colimits, in a step the author states is omitted with a hint, to reduce to the case where N is annihilated by some I^n (proof lines 24125-24129). It then introduces the square-zero extension R' = R/I^n oplus N and observes that it suffices to show the object K' = K tensor^L_R R' of D(R') has vanishing cohomology in positive degrees (proof lines 24130-24133). The substantive step is the passage along the surjection R' -> R/I with nilpotent kernel J: the proof computes K tensor^L_R R/I = (K tensor^L_R R') tensor^L_{R'} R/I = K' tensor^L_{R'} R/I, notes that by hypothesis this complex has tor amplitude in (-infinity, 0], and invokes the tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent lemma to conclude (proof lines 24134-24144). Part (1) is then immediate from part (2), and part (3) follows from part (2) by induction on the number of nonzero cohomology modules of M and the truncation distinguished triangles, in a final step the author again states is omitted (proof lines 24146-24151). The non-routine content is the square-zero extension trick and the transfer of the vanishing through the nilpotent quotient.
